$comment: Known divergences from the reference implementation (HMD-0020, Conformance, canonicity, and the drift ledger). Each entry names something this implementation is expected to get wrong, and why: `cases` are conformance cases, `rules` are lint rules it does not emit at all, `rendering` is HTML that differs. An entry that stops diverging fails the build — a ledgered case that PASSES, or a ledgered rule this implementation actually emits — because an expected failure that starts succeeding and is not removed is how a ledger rots into a lie.

cases.reason: The publication model is unported, so a published card linking to or embedding an unpublished one raises no HMD017; see HMD017 under `rules`. The case's resolutions agree.

rules.reason: The publication model behind it is unported. This implementation validates `nav` (a malformed one is HMD013), but does not act on `visibility`: it does not inherit it from folder notes, has no notion of a card being published, and so emits no HMD017 anywhere. Parity therefore drops HMD017 from the canonical side before comparing; every other rule is still compared.

rendering.reason: Raw HTML in a card is escaped rather than passed through. Deliberate: a webview rendering workspace HTML is a script-injection surface reachable from any cloned repository.
`~x~` subscript is unsupported; markdown-it's builtin only covers `~~strikethrough~~`.
Math is typeset by KaTeX here and by whatever MathJax the MkDocs site loads there. Both render the same LaTeX; the HTML around it differs.
